blogs.title: Presidential Power vs. Congressional Statutes: The Ninth Circuit’s Deference in Pacito v. Trump
blogs.description: This post will dissect the panel’s majority opinion that upholds the President’s authority under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(f) to suspend refugee admissions, examining the legal standards for deference in immigration cases, the application of Trump v. Hawaii, and the implications for future executive actions that invoke national‑security justifications.

blogs.title: Is Refugee Resettlement Funding Mandatory? A Deep Dive into the Statutory Interpretation Fight in Pacito v. Trump
blogs.description: Focusing on Judge Lee’s partial dissent, this article will analyze the competing readings of 8 U.S.C. § 1522—whether it imposes a binding duty or merely an authorization for refugee assistance—and explore how this debate could shape the scope of congressional mandates versus executive discretion in immigration‑related spending.

blogs.title: The Role of the APA in Immigration Policy: Why the Ninth Circuit Finds the Government Likely to Lose on Procedural Grounds
blogs.description: This piece will examine the court’s finding that, despite likely success on the merits of the executive‑order challenge, the government may falter on Administrative Procedure Act claims, assessing the standards for lawful agency action, the requirement of notice and comment, and how the APA can serve as a check on abrupt policy shifts.

blogs.title: Staying Orders and the Balance of Harms: How the Ninth Circuit Applied the Nken Factors in Pacito v. Trump
blogs.description: Analyzing the stay order issued by the Ninth Circuit, this blog will explain the four‑factor test from Nken v. Holder, assess how the court weighted irreparable injury, likelihood of success, and public‑interest considerations in the refugee context, and consider the broader impact on future emergency stays in immigration litigation.
